With string-valued maps this expresses exact finite equality. Type admission is absent: expected {a: None} and observed {} pass the .get comparison, so missing and explicitly null values collapse. Returned dicts are mutable despite the frozen wrapper. No actual Git observation is established.
122: PrincipalEvidenceV1 explicitly supplies syntax-checked references to an injected external verifier. Identifier roles, signature-digest shape, and allowed scheme labels are checked; cryptographic verification and principal trust are intentionally outside this record. Reuse as an evidence envelope only, preserving that stated boundary.
123: N1 qualification is a deterministic synthetic lifecycle harness: it appends LEASED/BOUND without obtaining a lease/binding, uses fixed epochs and promised base as observed base, records LANDED without Git mutation, defaults observed blobs to expected blobs, and appends disposal/pruning labels without performing them. It can exercise finite refusal branches, but its complete-lifecycle language is not operational end-to-end evidence. Receipt hash binds labels/states/head, not the complete content and write-scope population.
124: N2 qualification constructs two disjoint declared packets, simulates stale-head refusal and conservative rebind, then grants a fresh license after a comment asserting fresh evidence without invoking an evidence executor. Fixed epochs, local mutex, promised-as-observed blob defaults and absent Git/agent/human execution make this a finite scenario harness. The receipt digest omits the full candidate/content population; no concurrent production qualification follows.
125: N4 qualification counts supplied admissions/collisions and compares second/fourth patch-digest labels. Expected scenario outcomes are not asserted, equal empty digest strings are accepted, and the fourth admitted packet is not registered. The digest covers aggregate counters rather than the input population. Useful scenario accounting, not demonstrated four-worker isolation or enforced N4 success.
126: QuorumThreshold checks a 0.5-to-1 interval and positive minimum via comparisons, without exact-type or finiteness admission; NaN bypasses the interval comparisons. The already read council bridge independently revalidates thresholds, so this constructor weakness is not an end-to-end council bypass. Default 0.66 is the declared policy value, not exact two-thirds.
127: Rebind-after-merge marks each active obligation stale and always returns ready_to_land=False, including unchanged heads or no obligations. This is a useful conservative invalidation record, not an actual branch rebase, evidence refresh, or land-license gate.
128: ReceiptValidationError carries code/detail for typed refusal. It implements no receipt validation or custody policy itself.
129: Three-way reconciliation is an explicit ownership-first policy. Current actor ownership always chooses branch, even when only main changed; foreign ownership always chooses main, even when only branch changed. Only unowned paths use ordinary base/branch/main equality rules and otherwise yield UNRESOLVED. This is reusable if ownership is admitted as authority, not generic conflict-free preservation. Ledger hashing sorts all declared fields but neither authenticates ownership nor rejects duplicate paths.
130: RevalidateResult is an unchecked frozen ok/residual/live record. It carries a comparison result without independently observing or validating live state.
131: ReviewPin is an unchecked PR-number/head-SHA carrier; no remote lookup or content binding is supplied.
132: Review-worktree pinning rejects empty SHA and compares exact supplied head labels. It neither creates a worktree nor fetches the PR, checks tree contents, or binds review rules. Useful equality guard under a trusted observation port.
133: RuntimeEvent validates nonempty event/run/subject labels and shallow-freezes metadata. Its stated observational role is useful separation from authority, but nested metadata can mutate and the record does not authenticate the described fact.
134: SemanticContract rejects subclasses and delegates authority-effect fencing, but its ID is unchecked and no semantic predicate is executed. Equality-based conditional normalization leaves direct string None unchanged because the string enum compares equal to that string; the factory normalizes it. No authority escalation follows because only the NONE effect is admitted.
135: StepLimitExceeded is an exception leaf; step accounting and enforcement must occur at an external caller.
136: N10 skeleton honestly disclaims full production DoD and runs a serial synthetic scenario with fixed epochs and fabricated head labels. Its active-write map is keyed by candidate ID: repeated IDs with disjoint paths overwrite entries, so the dictionary count can stay below n_ceiling while the admitted list grows arbitrarily. Missing per-candidate observations default to promised blobs. is_successful is always True even with zero admitted candidates. Reuse as a scenario scaffold only after unique-ID admission and explicit success criteria.
137: Recovery playbook is a deterministic hashed dry-run plan, not an executor. Orphan leases, detached worktrees, and head drift map to declared actions; dirty-prune planning lacks data custody checks. UNBACKED_PR is encoded with RELEASE_ORPHAN_LEASE even though its target/description concerns a PR, a semantic dispatch mismatch if a consumer trusts action_type. Unknown drift kinds are refused. No planned action was executed.
138: SwarmRuntimeError is the base exception for explicit runtime failures, with no operational semantics of its own.
139: Swarm status reconciliation compares supplied packet membership with lease/worktree/PR bindings, emits finite orphan/detached/unbacked records, and hashes the entire supplied mapping population. HEAD_DRIFT exists as a tag but is never detected here because no second head observation is compared. The returned snapshot discards the original binding maps, so its serialized form alone cannot reconstruct its digest. This is caller-relative accounting, not an authoritative remote census.
140: SwarmTaskLimitExceeded names a bounded-task refusal but performs no task counting itself.
141: Task validates ID, goal, and optional capability labels and shallow-freezes payload. It is an admitted work description, not policy enforcement, deep immutability, or a proof the goal is executable.
142: TerminalStatusV1 explicitly names OPEN_OBSTRUCTION and REFUSED. These useful non-success labels do not implement an obstruction proof calculus.
143: ToolCall validates nonempty call/tool labels and shallow-freezes arguments. Allowed-tool resolution, argument schema validation, rate/capability checks, and execution remain external; nested arguments remain mutable.
144: ToolNotFound is an exception leaf; no tool registry or resolver exists in this file.
145: ToolResult is an unchecked result envelope containing arbitrary content and an is_error flag. It does not authenticate execution or validate correlation to a tool call.
146: Universal transport classification now explicitly refuses absent digests for claims about bytes and gives same-path/same-digest NOT_APPLICABLE; relocation cannot be NOT_APPLICABLE through the constructor. This repairs the documented unmeasured-to-verified branch at the declared-record level. VERIFIED still means predicates over supplied labels: empty or malformed non-None digests pass, redirect/deletion are caller flags, and no bytes/existence/redirect semantics are observed. Direct constructor admits inconsistent VERIFIED shapes except its one locus invariant. Useful mutation-evidence classifier with an external measurement and canonical-digest admission requirement.
147: UnsafeGitAddress is a ValueError with a default residual string. It supports typed refusal from the separately reviewed Git-address owner, not independent parsing.
148: Compatibility export surface delegates all listed IDs, digests, paths, timestamps, fences, epochs and mutation records to the shared kernel already fully read in this scope. The complete imports and __all__ were read. No separate mathematical mechanism or stronger guarantees arise from the swarm-control namespace.
149: Five-line compatibility re-export of shared-kernel Digest. It retains the same lexical digest admission and its limitations; no new digest implementation.
150: Five-line compatibility re-export of DigestKind. It adds no algorithm or constructor enforcement.
151: Five-line compatibility re-export of DomainInvariantError. It adds no validation behavior.
152: Five-line compatibility re-export of Epoch. The shared-kernel exact value semantics are inherited, not independently implemented.
153: Five-line compatibility re-export of FenceToken. It adds no durable fencing authority or monotone allocator.
154: Five-line compatibility re-export of IdKind. It adds no namespace or trust policy.
155: Five-line compatibility re-export of Identifier. Shared-kernel label checks remain the only implementation.
156: Five-line compatibility re-export of MutationAction. It adds no action execution or mutation admission.
157: Five-line compatibility re-export of MutationItemV1. It retains the reviewed constructor boundary limitations and does not create a second checker.
158: Six-line compatibility re-export of MutationManifestV1 and compute_manifest_sha256. The same NUL-delimited preimage encoding is used; this is not an independent integrity mechanism.
159: Five-line compatibility re-export of RepoPath and RepositoryPath. It inherits the shared lexical path admission rather than the different runtime path_canon helper.
160: Five-line compatibility re-export of TimestampUtc and UtcTimestamp. No new timezone normalization or canonical serialization is introduced.
161: WindowDeclaration admits only the NONE authority effect and rejects subclasses, with exact-type equality/hash. Direct string None can remain a string because equality rather than identity decides assignment; factory creation canonicalizes. The name is unchecked and the declaration does not actually enforce a time window. It is a label fence, not scheduling or authorization.
162: Work-packet mapping validation requires named fields, nonempty primary labels, nonempty write-path tuple, string sequence elements and the NONE effect; it trims primary labels. It does not validate SHA shape, canonical/unique paths, write-versus-forbidden conflicts, or empty individual path strings, and ignores supplied schema/unknown fields. Direct dataclass construction checks only exact class and authority effect, bypassing those mapping checks. Thus this is an input-shape adapter, not a closed work-scope or concurrency certificate.
163: WorkPacketValidationError carries the mapping-validator residual string. It has no admission or enforcement behavior outside that error envelope.
